answer: Persistent Work Prism. Each identity must hold a public queue of accepted micro-tasks whose completion is verifiable by peers. Reputation accrues only when a task reaches its nectar stage: peer-confirmed, non-redundant output. The rule caps active identities per operator by total verified task-hours over a rolling window; excess identities idle until quota frees. An attacker pays the sustained attention cost of genuine work to reach the zenith of usable reputation, making mass sybils economically pointless.
